title: Unauthorized access to student assignment data in transit
description: Student's work file, student ID, course, and submission timestamp could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission to the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Unintended disclosure of student information
description: Student data could be inadvertently disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or security breaches.

title: Inaccurate student submission data
description: Student may submit incorrect, incomplete, or outdated information, affecting the integrity and reliability of the grading system.

title: Potential privacy regulation violation
description: Student data handling may not comply with educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding student information protection.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if specific regulatory requirements are fully implemented

title: Accidental deletion of student submissions
description: Student assignment data could be accidentally or maliciously deleted from the Grades Portal Web App storage system.

title: Data Leakage During Transmission
description: Student data (student id, course, file reference, requesting role) may be intercepted or leaked during transmission from Grades Portal Web App to Assignment & Grading Service.

title: Unauthorized Information Disclosure
description: Sensitive student information including student ID, course details, and file references may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the routing process.

title: Unauthorized Access to Data
description: Data transmitted from Portal to Assignment & Grading Service may be accessed by unauthorized parties during transit.

title: Non-Repudiation of Submission
description: There may be issues proving which student actually submitted the work through the portal, as the routing process may not maintain proper audit trails.

title: Data Quality Issues During Transmission
description: Student data may be corrupted, incomplete, or altered during the routing process from Portal to Assignment & Grading Service.

title: Data Destruction During Transmission
description: Student data may be lost or destroyed during the transmission process from Portal to Assignment & Grading Service.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: The data routing process may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding student data transmission.

title: Legitimate Purpose for Data Processing
description: The grading service may process student assignment data without a clear, documented legitimate purpose or without obtaining proper consent from students.

title: Lack of Notice for Data Collection
description: Students may not be adequately informed about what data is being collected, stored, and how it will be used by the grading service.

title: Information Accuracy and Integrity
description: Student assignment data may be corrupted, altered, or inaccurate during the storage process, affecting the integrity of academic records.

title: Inadequate Data Destruction
description: Student assignment data may not be securely deleted when no longer needed, potentially leading to unauthorized access to past submissions.

title: Unintended Data Collection
description: The grading service may collect additional student data beyond what is necessary (e.g., IP address, device information) without proper justification.

title: Data Quality During Storage
description: Assignment files may be corrupted or degraded during storage in the Assignment Store, compromising data quality.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The Assignment Store may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding student data storage and retention.

title: Teacher login credentials intercepted during transmission
description: Teacher's login credentials could be intercepted by malicious actors during transmission to the Grades Portal Web App, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the system.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission without encryption

title: Student submission data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Student submission data containing personal information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, system vulnerabilities, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Assumes submissions contain identifiable student information

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: The Grades Portal Web App may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding the handling of student personal information during the submission review process.
assumptions: Assumes the system processes identifiable student data

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Personal Information
description: Student names and potentially sensitive work content are displayed to teachers who may not have a legitimate need to access this information, creating a confidentiality risk.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Student Data
description: Student submission data (names, work content, submission times) is being disseminated to teachers without proper access controls, potentially leading to unintended disclosure of sensitive student information.

title: Uncontrolled Data Dissemination
description: Student data is being disseminated from the portal to teachers without adequate controls on who can access or view the information, creating potential privacy risks.

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Student Information Display
description: The information displayed to teachers may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, potentially affecting the teacher's ability to properly evaluate student work.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Data During Transmission
description: Teacher's grade and feedback data could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission to the Grades Portal Web App, potentially exposing sensitive student information.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Student Information
description: Student ID and grader ID could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the data flow, potentially leading to privacy violations and identity exposure.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Transmission
description: Grade and feedback data could be altered or tampered with during transmission to the Grades Portal Web App, potentially leading to inaccurate records.

title: Non-repudiation of Grade Submission
description: Teacher may be unable to prove they submitted the grade and feedback, potentially leading to disputes about the authenticity of the recorded data.

title: Data Quality Issues in Grade Recording
description: The Grades Portal Web App may record inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading grade and feedback data due to input validation issues or system errors.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records containing student personal information (student id, course, grade, feedback) could be accessed by unauthorized personnel who do not have appropriate clearance to view student grades.

title: Inaccurate Grade Data Entry
description: Grades or feedback could be entered incorrectly due to human error, system malfunction, or data entry mistakes, compromising the accuracy of student records.

title: Lack of Non-repudiation for Grading Actions
description: Without proper audit trails and digital signatures, it may be difficult to verify who performed grading actions and when, potentially allowing denial of grading responsibilities.

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Grade records could be modified or corrupted during storage in the database, potentially altering student grades without detection.

title: Accidental Disclosure of Grade Information
description: Grade records could be inadvertently shared with unauthorized parties through system errors, misconfigured access controls, or improper data handling procedures.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations
description: The grading process may not fully comply with educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding student data protection and handling requirements.

title: Unauthorized access to student grades
description: Grades and feedback may be accessed by unauthorized parties during the retrieval process, potentially compromising student privacy

title: Inaccurate or outdated grades
description: Grades and feedback may not be accurate or up-to-date, affecting the student's ability to make informed decisions

title: Limited control over retrieved grades
description: Student may have limited control over how retrieved grades are stored, shared, or used after the initial retrieval

title: Accidental disclosure of grades
description: Grades may be accidentally shared with unauthorized parties through system errors, misconfigurations, or user mistakes

title: Unauthorized Modification of Student Grades
description: Grades and teacher feedback displayed to the student could be modified or tampered with without the student's knowledge or consent, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: The system may lack proper access controls or audit mechanisms to prevent unauthorized modifications.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Student Grades
description: Student grades and teacher feedback could be inadvertently disclosed to unauthorized users or parties outside the intended recipient (the student).
assumptions: The portal may have insufficient access controls or authentication mechanisms to prevent unauthorized access.

title: Inaccurate or Outdated Student Information
description: The grades and teacher feedback displayed to the student may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, affecting the student's ability to make informed decisions.
assumptions: The system may lack proper validation mechanisms or regular updates to ensure data accuracy.

title: Uncontrolled Data Dissemination
description: The dissemination of student grades and teacher feedback from the portal to the student may not be properly controlled, potentially leading to data leakage or improper distribution.
assumptions: The system may lack proper data flow controls or monitoring mechanisms.

title: Unauthorized access to child's grades
description: Parent may access grades of other children or unauthorized parties may access the system without proper authentication controls.
assumptions: Parent account is linked to child account but authentication may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access.

title: Excessive data collection
description: Grades portal may collect more personal information than necessary to provide grades, including unnecessary personal details about the child.
assumptions: System collects parent and child information beyond what is required for grade access.

title: Inaccurate or outdated grade data
description: Grade information may be incorrect, incomplete, or not updated in a timely manner, affecting the parent's ability to make informed decisions.
assumptions: Grades are stored in a database that may have synchronization issues or entry errors.

title: Insufficient notice of data usage
description: Parent may not be adequately informed about how their child's grade data is collected, used, and shared with third parties.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not be prominently displayed or may be difficult to understand.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Grades portal may not fully comply with applicable privacy laws and regulations regarding student data protection.
assumptions: System may not have proper privacy governance or may not keep up with changing regulations.

title: Disclosure of child's academic information to parents
description: The Grades Portal Web App displays child's grades, feedback, and submission history to parents. This could result in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal information if access controls are not properly implemented or if data is shared beyond intended recipients.

title: Unauthorized access to child's academic data
description: There is a risk that unauthorized individuals (e.g., other parents, unauthorized users) could access the portal and view the child's grades, feedback, and submission history through improper authentication or session management.

title: Inappropriate information sharing with parents
description: The portal may share information with parents that is not appropriate or necessary for their role, potentially including information that should remain private or shared only with specific consent.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: The data flow may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding the sharing of children's personal and academic information with parents.

title: Incorrect or incomplete personal data entry
description: School Administrator may enter inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated information when creating, modifying, or disabling accounts and parent-child links, leading to poor data quality that affects system functionality and decision-making.
assumptions: Administrator has access to input forms and validation mechanisms

title: Excessive data collection for account management
description: Administrator may collect more personal information than necessary for account and relationship management, potentially including unnecessary personal details about students or parents.
assumptions: No data minimization controls are in place

title: Lack of transparency in data processing
description: Users (students, parents) may not be adequately informed about how their personal information is being used when accounts and relationships are managed by the administrator.
assumptions: No clear privacy notices or consent mechanisms exist

title: Duplicate or conflicting parent-child relationships
description: Administrator may create duplicate accounts or inconsistent parent-child relationships, leading to confusion about which student or parent is being referred to and potential data integrity issues.
assumptions: No validation or deduplication mechanisms exist

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance
description: Data processing activities may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding student and parent data handling, consent, and data protection requirements.
assumptions: No legal compliance review or documentation exists

title: Unclear legal basis for data processing
description: The legal justification for collecting and processing student and parent information may not be clearly established or documented, raising questions about lawfulness of data processing activities.
assumptions: No documented legal basis or policy exists

title: Improper account or relationship deletion
description: When administrator disables accounts or removes parent-child links, there may be insufficient safeguards to ensure proper data destruction or archival, potentially leading to data loss or inability to recover important information.
assumptions: No data retention or archival policies exist

title: Unauthorized modification of account records
description: The grading service may allow unauthorized personnel to modify account records and parent-child relationship links, potentially altering sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has appropriate access controls in place.

title: Unauthorized access to account directory
description: Account records containing personal information may be accessed by unauthorized parties who should not have access to student or parent data.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory has proper access controls.

title: Inaccurate account information
description: The grading service may write incorrect or outdated account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory, leading to data quality issues.
assumptions: Assumes proper validation and verification processes exist.

title: Lack of notification about data usage
description: Users may not be adequately informed about how their account data is being used, stored, or shared within the grading service system.
assumptions: Assumes there is a notification mechanism in place.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: The data collection and storage practices of the grading service may not comply with applicable privacy laws and regulations regarding personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the organization is aware of and follows relevant privacy regulations.

title: Unauthorized Data Leakage to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted to an external cloud hosting provider, creating risk of unauthorized access or data leakage during transmission or storage.

title: Data Confidentiality Risk with Third-Party Storage
description: Sensitive student/employee data (grades, assignments, account directory) stored on third-party cloud infrastructure may be accessed by unauthorized parties or cloud provider employees.

title: Data Integrity Risk During Cloud Transfer
description: Data integrity may be compromised during nightly backup and replication to cloud hosting provider, with potential for corruption or tampering.

title: Data Availability Risk with Third-Party Cloud
description: Data availability may be compromised if cloud hosting provider experiences outages, service disruptions, or fails to maintain backup systems.

title: Data Protection Compliance Risk
description: Sharing sensitive data with third-party cloud provider may create compliance issues with data protection regulations (GDPR, FERPA, etc.) regarding data transfer and storage.
